locations.title: Baakline
locations.public_description: Modern Lebanese town in Chouf district (Mount Lebanon); Syriac origin meaning place of knots and turns.

locations.title: Bechamoun
locations.public_description: Modern Lebanese town in Aley district (Mount Lebanon); Aramaic origin meaning Temple of Eshmun. Direct survival of the Phoenician Eshmun cult name in the modern landscape.

locations.title: Brummana
locations.meaning: House of Rammana, god of air, storm, thunder
locations.public_description: Modern Lebanese town in Matn district (Mount Lebanon); Aramaic origin meaning House of Rammana, a god of air, storm, and thunder.

locations.title: Bsharre
locations.public_description: Modern Lebanese town in Mount Lebanon (Bsharre district); Phoenician origin Bet Ishtar meaning house of Ishtar. The strongest single survival of Ishtar / Inanna's name in the modern Lebanese landscape.

locations.title: Dar Baachtar
locations.public_description: Modern Lebanese town in Koura district (North Lebanon); Phoenician origin meaning home of worship of Astarte. Direct survival of Astarte's name in the modern landscape.

locations.title: Ehden
locations.public_description: Modern Lebanese town in Zgharta district (North Lebanon); Phoenician origin for the word Eden, meaning paradise or garden.

locations.title: Hammana
locations.meaning: stone pillar to worship the sun
locations.public_description: Modern Lebanese town in Baabda district (Mount Lebanon); Phoenician origin from Hammon, a pre-monotheistic solar deity associated with stone pillars.

locations.title: Berytus
locations.public_description: Phoenician coastal city; ancient name from the root for "wells." Roman-era Berytus housed one of the most prestigious law schools of the ancient Mediterranean. Modern Beirut is the present-day capital of Lebanon and the implicit setting for Ard Ba'alat's contemporary timeline.

locations.title: Byblos
locations.public_description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Major Phoenician port and the historical center of the Baalat Gebal (Lady of Byblos) and Adonis cults. The Greek name "Byblos" gave rise to the word for book (papyrus was traded through here).

locations.title: Sidon
locations.public_description: One of the oldest and most important Phoenician city-states. Major center of glass-making and dye production. Anchor of the Eshmun cult, whose temple complex sits just north of the city.

locations.title: Tripoli
locations.meaning: Three Cities (Greek renaming of the original Phoenician name Athar)
locations.public_description: Northern Phoenician coastal city. Originally called Athar; the current name "Tripoli" (three cities) is a Greek renaming reflecting the federation of three separate quarters founded by colonists from Tyre, Sidon, and Aradus.

locations.title: Tyre
locations.public_description: One of the most ancient and powerful Phoenician city-states. Famous for the Tyrian purple dye industry and as the founding city of Carthage. Major Mediterranean trade hub from the second millennium BCE onward.
